706790.t: PIE word *h₁éḱwos From Proto-Hellenic *íkkʷos (compare Mycenaean Greek 𐀂𐀦 (i-qo)), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁éḱwos, from *h₁oh₁ḱu- (“swift”).

706772.t: From Ἰουδά (Ioudá) + -ιος (-ios), from Biblical Hebrew יְהוּדָה (Yəhūḏā(h), “Judah”).

706747.t: The stem ἵ- (hí-) is probably from Proto-Indo-European *Hyós (“that, who, which”), while the ending is an instrumental ending found in Sanskrit येन॑ (yéna, “by which; by that”), Old High German hina (“thither”), Old Irish cen (“on this side”).

706764.t: From Proto-Hellenic *ihwós, a thematicization of Proto-Indo-European *(H)isu- (“arrow”). Cognates include Sanskrit इषु (íṣu, “arrow”) and Avestan 𐬌𐬱𐬎 (išu, “arrow”).

706723.t: Stem ἱλα- as in ἱλάσκομαι (hīlắskomai, “to appease”), ἵλαος (hílaos, “gracious”) + -ρός (-rós).

706728.t: From the reduplicated *si-sl̥h₂-sḱetor, from Proto-Indo-European *selh₂- (“mercy, comfort”). By surface analysis, ἵλαος (hī́laos, “propitious, gracious”) + -σκω (-skō).

706710.t: From the root of ἱκνέομαι (hiknéomai, “to be appropriate”) + -νος (-nos).

706789.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *HéHḱus Proto-Indo-European *h₁éḱwos Proto-Hellenic *íkkʷos Ancient Greek ἵππος (hĭ́ppos) Proto-Indo-European *drem- Proto-Indo-European *-os Proto-Hellenic *-os Ancient Greek -ος (-os) Ancient Greek δρόμος (drómos)…

706718.t: ἱκνέομαι (hĭknéomai, “to come”) + -της (-tēs, “-er”, masculine agent-noun suffix): literally, “comer”.

706786.t: From ἵππος (hĭ́ppos, “horse”) + -εύς (-eús, suffix for masculine person concerned).

706732.t: Variant of ἵλαος (hī́laos, “auspicious, favorable”) formed after the pattern ναός (nāós) : νεώς (neṓs), λαός (lāós) : λεώς (leṓs).

706719.t: From Proto-Indo-European *seykʷ- (“to filter”) and cognate with Old English sēon (“to filter”), Russian сцать (scatʹ, “to piss”) and Sanskrit सिञ्चति (siñcáti, “to pour”). Beekes suggests *seyk- as the original root.

706733.t: Perhaps a nominal formation from ἴλλω (íllō, “to press together”), from Proto-Indo-European *wi-wl-e, a reduplicative formation from Proto-Indo-European *wel- (“to press together”), whence also εἴλω (eílō, “to shut in, press”); see there for more discussion.

706741.t: As a secondary formation in -ντ- (-nt-), presupposes a noun *ἱμα (*hĭmā) or *ἱμα (*hĭmă) meaning "rope", which is also continued in ἱμάω (hĭmắō), ἱμάσθλη (hĭmắsthlē) and ἱμαῖος (hĭmaîos).

706736.t: Formation like ἀχλύς (akhlús) and δελφύς (delphús). Identical with Proto-Slavic *jьlъ (“silt; clay”) and Latvian īls (“very dark”).

706720.t: The formation is reminiscent of ὕδερος (húderos) and χολέρα (kholéra), but further details are unknown.
